text: curious how that translates to props that are built from mesh outliners. Since the prop is quite arbitrary, how exactly does the packed buffer affect this, and i guess worth asking how is it as it stands now. Is it for the entire model? or something else ?
resolution: Question-only ask, no code changed. Explained how the packed 20-byte Vertex relates to outliner-built props: an outliner model is ONE concatenated vertex stream on the host (parts are contiguous ranges — metadata, not separate buffers); placement registers the whole model once as a resident mesh keyed by FNV hash (meshProps.ts -> world_loader scene3d_geom_key -> internGeometry), so the packing applies per-vertex to that single shared GPU copy at upload; each placement stays a 32-byte InstanceData row referencing it. Arbitrary shapes are unaffected because positions stay full f32 — only normals (oct, ~0.003 deg) and UVs (f16, ~1-texel worst case at a 4096 atlas edge, absorbed by island gutters) are quantized. Live mesh-editor drafts stream through the same pack at the dyn-slot upload boundary.
